overview: This 531-page file traces American and British oil companies’ negotiations with Japan over the Petroleum Industry Law from 1935 to early 1936. Embassy reports, company proposals, meeting records, telegrams, and departmental memoranda document disputes over compulsory reserves, sales quotas, refining, prices, and tariffs, alongside Japanese efforts to secure oil supplies abroad.
interest: Detailed meeting records reveal how oil companies, diplomats, and Japanese ministries negotiated commercial rights amid strategic supply concerns.
